rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a combined computational framework coupling ab initio phonon and Boltzmann transport calculations, while the target uses Monte Carlo and non-equilibrium molecular dynamics to induce chemical short-range order. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (computational methodology vs. structural modification).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies experimental conditions (50–1200 K, controlled atmosphere, low-strain heat flow) and computational conditions (ab initio, Boltzmann transport), whereas the target uses atomistic simulation (Monte Carlo, molecular dynamics) with a single-phase bcc constraint. The regimes are different (experimental validation vs. pure simulation).
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis mechanism relies on decoupling phonon and electron transport and using full spectrum ab initio calculations to improve prediction accuracy. The target mechanism involves SRO reducing lattice distortion and creating percolation pathways that increase lattice heat conductivity. These are different general classes of mechanism (transport decoupling vs. structural ordering effects).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts total thermal conductivity within ±10% of experiments and a crossover in transport mechanism near 200 K. The target predicts a ~12% increase in lattice heat conductivity due to SRO. The hypothesis does not predict the specific outcome of the target (SRO-induced conductivity increase).
